column4: Pixel-art sprites in the style of 1990s Build-engine games (Duke Nukem 3D, Redneck Rampage): digitized and crudely retouched by hand, flat even lighting, chunky pixels, a limited muddy palette, low saturation, seen straight on from the front. A sprite sheet: 2 separate objects in one row from left to right, each one whole, all at the same scale, with wide gaps of background between them so none touch. The background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere, no cast shadows, no table, no text, no labels, no letters, no border, no watermark. Every object is drawn big and simple so it still reads when it is shrunk to sixteen pixels tall: plain shapes, bold dark outlines, flat fills of two or three colours. The objects, left to right: a big heavy jute sack, full and lumpy, slumped on its side, its neck twisted shut with rusty wire, coarse brown weave, its bottom damp and darker; a battered dented steel tray heaped with fresh coarse-minced red meat.
